utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. If I could remind you, Mr. Zorc, of the affirmation which you took at the beginning of your evidence, which still applies. Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Good morning, General. Good morning, counsel. I would first like to point out a transcript error which needs immediate attention from page 53, line 20. I believe the word "not" was omitted. It basically starts at 17 and it reads: "The subordinates must feel that the requirements of the superiors and the regulations" - I'm sorry - "of superiors and the requirements of military relationships and military organisation and regulations are serious and that the violations of these military relationships" -- the transcript reads "be tolerated." I'm confident it should be "are not to be tolerated." There were several other corrections, but I can submit them in writing. They were mainly typographical, numbers of articles that were subsequently shown to be correct but appeared incorrectly perhaps in one line. Examined by Ms. Somers: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, yesterday we were discussing how criminal proceedings would be instituted or implemented, and when we left off, just to refresh you, my last question to you was: Do I understand you correctly: He must ensure that the information is communicated? Is that correct? And you indicated yes. And that was about the obligation, the responsibility of the commander of the operational group with respect to facts or information concerning crimes allegedly committed by units under his command and control. I would ask that Exhibit P63, tab 9, I believe, from P60 --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Tab 39 from Exhibit P63 be shown. Is it possible to put it on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, in front of you is an exhibit which is a preliminary commission report concerning observations by individuals who are part of the 2nd Operational Group who went to a -- in this instance, it's Dubrovnik, but let's say the -- a scene where allegations of damage, criminal allegations of damage to cultural property had been lodged. I ask you to look at the paragraph before the ending. You have the Serbo-Croatian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm afraid the witness does not have the document in front of him at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Did we give you the wrong ... If we have -- my apologies. It is 6139. It is -- it is the December 9th commission report, and we gave you the wrong binder. I'm terribly sorry. If it would help, I'll just give my copy, if that makes it easier to work from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll get the exhibit. It's Exhibit 61?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes. 39.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Tab 9 or tab --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: 3-9. Yes, 3-9. Can I be of assistance? If you could put that -- the English version on the ELMO, please. And in particular, just so we make sure that you're looking at the same document in Serbo-Croatian, it's the document dated 9 December 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you had -- you have seen this document, have you not, in proofing session, General?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe you've shown it to me two days ago when I came to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... the last part above the signature area. And if the usher would be kind enough to put that second -- the last page on the ELMO. It is the opinion of the commission that no substantial damage to the cultural and historical monuments -- that there is no substantial damage to the cultural and historical monuments. The origin of all the damage, the origin of all the damage cannot be stated with certainty and the perpetrators named because it's obvious that a lot of damage was not caused by attacks from outside of the Old Town centre. If you are informed as the commander of the 2nd Operational Group that there are allegations made of criminal conduct by your units, and a preliminary inquiry is -- claims -- or produces what may be inconclusive, what would your -- what is the responsibility now where there -- it remains an allegation and there is no further clarification at the preliminary stage? What do you do?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do I understand correctly that you're asking me what do I think about this assessment of -- of Commander Jokic that there was no substantial damage to the historical monuments?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm asking you is: Where there are allegations of criminal conduct and the very initial inquiry, the very initial observations are inconclusive, yet the allegations remain, what do you do, as the commander of the 2nd Operational Group? Indication is the perpetrators have not been identified and origin of damage has not been identified.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, once the superior officer received this report, he could have, and he should have, acted against perpetrators irrespective whether the damage has been determined or not, and irrespective whether the damage is bigger or smaller. The protected monuments, it's prohibited to shell protected monuments. There is indication that damage did occur, and the allegation stands that the shelling occurred. And therefore, he should have acted against the perpetrators.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And based on your testimony yesterday, what steps would he undertake? What procedures would he next undertake, given that the allegations are allegations of criminal conduct?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In any case, even if he had not been convinced that such criminal action is taking place, he should - namely, all superior officers, even the highest, also the highest - should ensure primarily that such possible shelling be stopped immediately because it is prohibited. Therefore, it means that with the most speediest of means, he should issue an order to stop the shelling and order the stopping of the shelling. At the same time, he should ensure that in such a situation, that also the superior command be informed. In further actions, which he should undertake, the further actions will depend whether his order on the stopping of the shelling had been respected and whether the shelling had been stopped or not. In case the shelling stopped, he should act -- begin acting in order to ensure the -- to determine the responsibility of those who were responsible for this unlawful shelling. From his subordinates, he should immediately request an immediate report on -- concerning the event itself, and he should primarily determine who issued the order for the shelling and on the basis of whose order it took place, if it wasn't on the basis of his. And also why such shelling occurred. Therefore, he should request a report concerning the reasons, the purposes of shelling, the goals, the targets of shelling, and also the scope of shelling. He should also evaluate and request data concerning that, what was the military need to carry out the shelling of these protected monuments. While requesting this report, if he believed -- deemed it necessary, in view of the significance of the incident, he could send one of his officers directly to the unit which is allegedly the perpetrator of that act and who would assist in inquiring in these matters that I Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. indicated. At the same time, as he is aware that such alleged shelling was both against the provisions, the directions of -- the director of the general -- the secretary, federal secretary, and his order, so it's obviously a criminal act, and he should warn and send the organs of military police to send them in to investigate the aspects of criminal action. And with that, he would carry out the necessary activities for protecting evidence to take in the perpetrators, and via the military police also the military investigator would -- the military prosecutor would be informed. And with that, he would take steps in order for the punishment of perpetrators. Now, if the order -- his order to stop the shelling were not respected and the shelling had not stopped, he would not only repeat another issue, another order; he would have to, in view of the significance of such an incident for the armed forces and for the state, he would probably have to go personally to -- in the field, and with his own authority, stop the shelling.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, you are giving an answer that reflects both at the time of the violation -- at the time of the shelling and then subsequent to it an assessment of alleged damage. Now, one question: You -- the translation comes out as "should" with these various obligations. Is it "must"? Are these obligations that the commander ... It is part --

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the role of the system of command and control is to ensure that orders are implemented and provisions respected. Any action needed in this sense is fundamental for command and control functioning. Therefore, it is expected that each and every commander makes -- invests all his capabilities in this function of command. So from his commanding officers, it is to be expected that they will do that, and if not, they are considered that they are not performing their duty. And in this case, not in concrete terms, he should do -- he must stop the shelling and must hand over the perpetrators to the competent organs. If he succeeded in stopping that, it would be successful command and control, and if not, it would be unsuccessful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In the interests of time, and we have very limited time, I'm going to ask you some questions and ask for brief responses. I'll keep the questions brief, and the response, if I could ask, would be brief. And thank you very much for your comment. Now, one further comment or question on this document. The document is addressed to Admiral Brovet. Does that suggest to you in any way that -- is that irregular in any way? Does that have any implications on the chain of command or that -- does it diminish in any way the position of the operational group commander?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is nothing extraordinary. The upper levels are allowed to have contacts with the levels two or three levels below them, and this was really a response to the request, and I believe that the commander of the 9th PVS [as interpreted] also sent a copy of this report to the commander of the 2nd Operational Group.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there's something missing in the transcript, I'm afraid. This is a response to a request made by the federal secretary. We are on page 7, line 15. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If a response -- as a follow-on to that, if the response came from the federal secretariat and was sent down to Admiral Jokic or -- I'm sorry, strike the name. To a subordinate commander, not the commander of the operational group, does that have any -- is that irregular, is that -- if it's one unit down from the commander of the operational group, is there any -- anything particularly irregular about that?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've mentioned already before that it's nothing extraordinary. It's allowed. It's possible. But it's not a fully regular procedure. The regular procedure is down along the steps of the chain of command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does -- however, by virtue of duty to be informed, does the commander of the operational group have to be informed of all the information coming from his units himself, whether his name appears on this document or not?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, he must be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When an operational group is formed and various formations or units are placed under -- are subordinated to it, in your experience, is it a norm -- a norm or a regular practice for commanders who are subordinated or -- I'm sorry - who are re-subordinated to the operational group to still retain some form of contact to their parent -- to their parent commanders? An example: If a commander of a naval military sector is redeployed and fully subordinated to the -- a 2nd Operational Group or an operational group commander, is it expected that that naval operational group commander will keep his parent commander informed of important events within the new formation?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the normal situation, because the re-subordinated units and units included in operational groups or tactical groups, they are withdrawn from their regular commands temporarily. Therefore, if a unit is attached to the temporary group, also its parent command expects that it will be returned after the operation is completed. Therefore, with the parent -- this contact with the parent command is something normal. But it doesn't represent the chain of command, the line of command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. Within the functions of the assistant commander for morale and legal affairs, is also -- is it also -- I'm sorry. Let me strike. Let me rephrase it. The function of the assistant commander for morale and legal affairs, is one of his functions also propaganda?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. In peace, in peacetime, this is considered information activity, while in war, this is called propaganda, and it is within the competence of this assistant commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which commander or which body collects, in combat, information about the enemy?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the intelligence body subordinated to the Chief of Staff of any command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The -- to whom were the military police in an operation group, to whom were the military police subordinated?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my apologies. I object to this kind of examination. The question should be: Does the operational group have any military police? If the answer to that question is yes, then we can have further clarification. Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can immediately answer this question. I just wanted to say that if, in the operational group, there was a unit of military police, then functionally it was subordinated to the intelligence body of the command of the operational group, and in the chain of command, the commander of the military police was directly subordinate to the commander of the operational group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Criminal offences are prosecuted in both times of peace and times of war, is that correct, within the military?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So any provisions of Article 241 of the Law on Service of the Armed Forces are -- which you have cited in your report on page 27 in the English, are those inapplicable to criminal activity, to crimes, such as shelling cultural monuments, unlawful attack against civilian population or civilian objects?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right. Article 241 of the law regulates disciplinary measures within the military organisation and does not apply to criminal prosecution.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is coordination a function of command and control?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Coordination of all units is an integral part of the function of command and control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the commander of an operational group have the authority to make his own decisions concerning the use of his units, subject to any possible direction from his superiors? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All commanders, any commander, in the implementation of the task assigned to him decides on the way his forces are engaged in the performance of such a duty, such a task.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Excuse me just a moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next question, if you do not know, please just indicate that you do not know and we'll move on quickly. Are you aware of the geographical boundaries in the zones of responsibility of the military naval district and the 9th Naval Sector, let's say in 1991? If you're not aware ...

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that within the competence of the 9th Military Naval Sector was the southern rim of the coast of the Adriatic Sea, however, without knowing the exact borders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would the boundaries affect the operations of the 2nd Operational Group?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that the borders between the sectors, military naval sectors, do not influence the operations of the 2nd Operational Group because the 2nd Operational Group was formed for the area of several corps, corps districts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. In the course of proofing, it became -- it arose that on page 25 of your English -- of the English report, there was some -- that the way it was formulated did not accurately reflect your intention, and you have submitted a paragraph clarifying. The report which has -- it begins with heading (b): "On the basis of your experience, were these measures sufficient in order to maintain discipline? If not, what kind of measures should the commander have adopted at corps level if the particular -- in particular, the commander of the 2nd operations [sic] group?" You have submitted a clarification, which says: "In my view, in the prevailing circumstances of combat, the 2nd Operational Group commanding officers had insufficient formal personal disciplinary powers to immediately punish in order to ensure the necessary level of discipline. Examples of the available powers [in relation to officers) include warning, reprimand, severe reprimand, and taking action in the military disciplinary courts. The powers are detailed more fully under the heading (iii), military discipline in the JNA, sub (a), disciplinary authority of the commanding officers in the JNA." Can you indicate what your purpose for clarifying was? Were you suggesting -- if you could just indicate, please.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my conversation with you and when I received, and that was only two days ago, when I had this insight for the first time into the English version, I became aware that your understanding of it was different as to what I wished to convey. Therefore, I provided this information in the English language so as to be understood in accordance with my purpose. As stated in my original report, namely, that the formal authorities of commanders in the operational group were not enough, and what I had in mind was the formal disciplinary competencies or authority or powers, which are insufficient. But I was not referring to their commanding authority, because obviously they had all these rights in regard to their forces. Hence my explanation, my clarification. This is what I have in mind, the disciplinary aspects. Therefore, their disciplinary competencies for in fact -- in order to be able to issue disciplinary measures, which in my mind are insufficient.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you -- and your emphasis on immediately, on immediate punishment was a factor you wanted to convey?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. What I had in mind was in fact the direct disciplinary measures and issuance of such measures against the subordinates and these measures can be issued immediately. And these are measures, disciplinary measures, for milder forms of breach of military discipline.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This does not have any impact on the powers, the authority, the obligation of the commander of an operational group to take all the measures at his disposal to make sure that criminal activity or disciplinary violations which are serious enough be dealt with; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is also -- just so the Chamber is aware, I believe on page 41, line 14 from yesterday's transcript, General Zorc was asked about disciplinary measures called for warning, and the translation of what he described as "reprimand" came out as "censure." Is warning -- is "reprimand" the term that is used in the -- in command and control parlance, "reprimand"?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is obviously the English, the English word used, but in my language, we say "ukor."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I just turn the Chamber's attention to page 14, I think it's remained in the most recent one of the English version where the language appears as "reprimand" and there's a difference simply in the in-court translation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Somers, could I raise with you: You have put to the witness that he made a correction to the paragraph which you referred on page 25 in English. Now, the Chamber does not have it. I don't say we must have it, but understand we don't. If you judge that it should be before us --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I do. And I had in mind, Your Honour -- thank you for your intervention. I had in mind to make sure that you have it. Because I would ask when I tender the report that you also have that in front of you. I'll have to get a signed -- a copy of the signed -- it was provided to the Defence and if I may at the break make sure that you have it, but I can give the unsigned and make sure you have the signed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You're welcome. Okay. Excuse me just a moment, I want to just ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, a question about the imposition of discipline or investigation of discipline -- alleged disciplinary violations and the impact of failure to undertake investigations of disciplinary violations. You have made -- you have used the concept that repeated violations could occur if, in the first instance, disciplinary measures were not implemented. I want to pose to you a scenario where, in the month of October of 1991 allegations of criminal conduct by units under an operational group were made. There was a general atmosphere of denial about the allegations, and assume there was a general atmosphere of denial about the allegations, and assume nothing is done. A month later, in November, there are again allegations with various levels of corroboration about the same conduct again by members of the same operational group. There is -- again, the assumption for you is that there is a general atmosphere of denial and that there is no further inquiry. If the operational group has a strategic order to implement negotiations subsequent to these two incidents I'm describing, what, if anything, would be the appropriate action of the commander of the operational group with respect to the units which were deemed to have committed the violations, the criminal violations that went uninvestigated?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not really know whether I have understood the question correctly and what implications does this have as regards the implementation of negotiations? Implementation of negotiations could be some sort of task, but has no relation to the implementation of command and control, and the implementation of the responsibility for incorrect behaviour of the subordinate officers. The implementation or the measures against the subordinates, due to their errors, in implementation of their tasks, should be carried out irrespective of any negotiations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. If problematic officers are left in place, what does that -- without any further control over their conduct by way of investigation of allegations, what does that signal about the conduct of those officers who are alleged to have behaved problematically?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The very fact that commanders committing certain errors remain at Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. their posts and act onwards doesn't mean anything else than it's been assessed that their activities are at least acceptable and that they can go onwards doing that, what they're doing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What security measures might you take as the commander of an operational group to ensure that a strategic goal of negotiations with a number of very important points takes place without incident?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is a question that I probably or maybe do not understand entirely. Well, security measures that are to provide for normal implementation of negotiations require at least that the team vested with the implementation of negotiations can safely and securely come to the venue of negotiations, have certain mandate and authority for doing that, and that regular communications are maintained with the team. As --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think I will -- just what measures -- let's remove the word "security." What measures would you undertake to make sure that everything is smooth and goes off as it is supposed to? If you are responsible to ensure that these negotiations happen and take place, what are the considerations as commander of an operational group that you would undertake? What measures?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if such a task had been vested with me, in my opinion, as the most important, I would select the most appropriate officers so as to implement these negotiations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How would you -- how would you make sure that the cease-fire that is part of it is respected? What would you do to make sure a cease-fire is respected?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I could have established cease-fire, of course I would have proposed that to the opposite side. However, if that was already suggested while the agreement on cease-fire was concluded, I would have made sure that my units wouldn't have conducted any activities. This -- the order should be given to the units and the deadline should be given to the units. And this should last until the time agreed or until the units get a new order from my part, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I would at this time request to tender into evidence the report, and I will also address a couple of other exhibits from the binder. But the report itself, if I may. And I will include, of course, the signed copy of the clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is this at tab 1?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The -- I believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We have two forms at tab 1, as well as -- in English, that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The filed one is there, sir, and the revised one, which should be filed by CLSS, but I was asked to have those submitted. They are in tab 1 of your binders. The original may be superfluous. If it would be helpful just to have the revised -- the translation, it might be burdensome, but I don't know if it has been filed by CLSS. Perhaps Madam Registrar can say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think at the moment we will receive the revised report, which is the one which the witness has been speaking to. It appears to be the first document at tab 1, but we will of course receive the original. Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence team would like to request the following, in view of the numerous problems that we've encountered, unfortunately, with Mr. Zorc's testimony being interpreted, to have the original of this report also admitted into evidence. And as far as I understand, the original was done in the Slovene language. We don't even have a copy of that, and we would like to have one, and we would like to have the original admitted into evidence. That is, after all, the original document, the B/C/S translation being, in a manner of speaking, a third-hand translation. I think the original text might come in useful in a number of different situations. Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do we have it available, Ms. Somers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes, it was offered to the Defence, I'm informed, and it was not at that time accepted. But yes, it is available and we're happy to provide it to the Defence. Does the Chamber wish to have a copy?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No. But if that is to happen, I think we ought to have the English language version of it, which is the second of the documents at tab 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: That's fine. Okay. Then we could include it as part of the submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will receive first the revised report in English at tab 1.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be P204.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will receive, secondly, the original report in the English translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be P205.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will receive - we will receive it at this moment, even though physically we are acting in anticipation - the original report in the Slovene language.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be P206.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The three versions in immediate proximity may be useful for later reference purposes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And upon -- the point -- the clarification I have only at this moment in the unsigned form but I would also ask that that be accepted as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be P207.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, there was one -- I believe one exhibit that remained from the binder that General Zorc made reference to in footnote 50, and it's the plan of damage from October, November 1991. Simply for the fact that it was in his report, we would include it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Which tab is this?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: It is tab 20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think tab 21 remains outstanding as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes, you're right. I'm sorry. 21 as well. But 20 was again mentioned in the footnote. I do not know the degree of reliance, but it is mentioned. And for that reason only, and nothing further ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that not an exhibit already?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I don't recall that it has a number. Unless in the course -- if that was one of the ones that Mr. -- that the Defence may have availed itself of. Our preliminary check did not show an exhibit number on it. I can get back to that, Your Honour, so that I don't delay the Chamber. I'll move on for a moment to tab 21, which is in footnote 52 of General Zorc's report. It's an order of General Adzic to the JNA regarding observation of international humanitarian law.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By your leave, in relation to the document at tab 21, at least in terms of its contents, I identified an exhibit that has already been admitted in relation to witness Jokic, and it was assigned a number at the time. At any rate, we object to this document at tab 25 [as interpreted] being admitted, because this is not an original document that was admitted into evidence before this Court during the testimony of witness Jokic. If I may remind you, this is an extract from a book that was shown at the time. It was a collection of documents shown by the Defence team to Admiral Jokic for him to identify in terms of the origin of those documents. Now suddenly a document with the same contents but with a different form of unknown origin shows up. There is no signature, there is no name for this document either. So we have no other choice but to object to this document at tab 21, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Somers. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the -- if the content is effectively the same and it exists in a different document, the exhibit number of which we are searching for, but -- and I think that there is no basis for the objection. Secondly, it was relied upon simply -- or it was mentioned in a footnote, and that is the purpose for its tendering. The weight of it is certainly always something the Chamber evaluates, but I think for completeness of the footnotes, so that the Chamber has before it whatever was cited in the report, it should be admitted and simply everything else goes to weight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So both the plan at tab 20 and the apparent order at tab 21, just at this moment, subject to anything that may have occurred earlier in the evidence - which isn't presently, to my mind, at least - are unverified documents, so their admission could only be to enable knowledge of what was relied on by this present witness in preparing his report, and not in any way of truth of the content of either of those documents. Is that the basis upon which you tender them?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes, it is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think on that basis, Mr. Rodic, we would receive both. But on their own at the moment on the evidence, they prove nothing except that this witness looked at them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Toward the conclusion of your examination, I wanted to ask you about your formal education. If you could indicate, please -- I'm sorry. I realised when I went through the transcript yesterday, I did not ask that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you indicate to the Chamber, General, what your formal education at the university level is. What degrees you hold and where you got them.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course I can do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. I'm sorry. Before you answer. I'm sorry, Your Honour. I pre-empted the issuance of exhibit numbers. I'm terribly sorry. Jumping ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I noted that. But, as usual, was letting you have your head.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: No, I wanted to make sure I was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will have the court officer receive those last two documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm sorry, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's okay. The map will be marked as P208, and the order will be marked as P209.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now the university education of the general.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General Zorc. If you could help us with that, please.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can list you points concerning my education. I have completed, as I already mentioned, the ground forces military academy of JNA in 1958.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... degrees. Is this -- is this education university level? Okay. Excuse me for interrupting you.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Military academy is on the level of university. Following the completed military academy, I completed the commanding staff military academy of military air force and air defence that I have completed in 1975. Then, in 1979, I graduated at the school of -- military school of People's Defence, and in the year 1967, at the highest school of general People's Defence. All these schools I have completed in Belgrade. In the course of my service, my active service, that is, I graduated in law at Ljubljana University.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time the Prosecution has completed its examination-in-chief. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Somers. Mr. Rodic, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. May I just have a moment, please, to organise myself before I begin my cross-examination. Cross-examined by Mr. Rodic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Zorc. My name is Goran Rodic. I represent General Strugar before this Tribunal. I will ask you questions in relation to your report and your testimony in chief. First of all, I'd like to ask you to tell me the following: When you drafted your expert report, what combat and operational documents did you study? Which type of document? Who gave them to you? Where did you study them?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Except for military regulations concerning the majority of questions put to me, I, on the occasion of a visit to this court in January this year, could see and get an insight into a number of military documents of the command of the 2nd Operational Group and the 9th Military Naval Sector, and as for the documents that I deemed important in the presentation of my view, well, as far as these documents are concerned, I did point them out in my report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The documents that you pointed out in your report, predominantly, except for the rules and legal provisions that you have pointed out, what I want to know about is the combat and operational documents. Are these documents that we can find in these binders? Have these documents been admitted into evidence here before this Court?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, from what I saw and was shown to me, these were some binders about their formal position and status at this Court. With this, I'm not acquainted. And the tabs were the tabs that I also quoted in my report. If that means that they were registered, this is what it means.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you to provide a specific answer, if you can, please. I'm talking about the documents -- this is a binder that the OTP has tendered into evidence, with exhibits in relation to your report, and these documents were shown to you yesterday and today, documents from this binder, from this tab, and these documents were also listed in the footnotes to your report; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. I haven't got this binder.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you can tell me, talking about these combat and operational documents, with the exception of those that you've referred to in the footnotes to your report, which other combat and operational documents have you studied?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in fact, some more documents were shown to me, and more documents that I actually used were shown to me. However, I have not studied them, except when I established that in a document there is anything of relevance helping me to answer the questions put to me. If that was the case, then I reviewed the document in question, then also took down the number of the document and followed by digits. That's the way they are in fact numbered. But without really knowing, I couldn't tell you what that means.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please: When was this rather large number of documents given to you which you used to identify the documents that you referred to in your report?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: May the witness please be asked to make a pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Immediately prior to my preparation of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me where it was that you had an opportunity to study these documents?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I studied all these documents at the Prosecutor's office here in The Hague in January.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to these documents that you have referenced in your report, can you perhaps remember any other combat or operational documents that you studied, something that remained with you?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall any other documents that would be relevant for my Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, did you have any working maps, for example, those belonging to the commander of the 2nd Operational Group? Did you look at any of those while drafting your report? Did you perhaps study JNA working maps?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And then I also came across such a map of the command of the 2nd Operational Group in January that was as well, in the same premises, at the same time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of maps were those?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were maps of the command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what was indicated on those maps?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. What was indicated there was the deployment of the forces of the 2nd Operational Group, of the corps, of the sector, then also some positions of some brigades, then also everything up to the line of the Neretva River and on the coast, to the positions to the south of Dubrovnik. And what was indicated was the command post of the 2nd Operational Group. Well, this is what I recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you perhaps remember any of the data on those maps?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were these maps important for you in the preparation of your report?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not particularly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, sir: During the drafting of your report, did you also use the interview that Admiral Jokic gave to the investigators of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This interview from the hearing, or something like that, I had the opportunity of seeing it then, here, and also I could review it very briefly within the short time available.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you also use in your report information or data that you found in the interview by Admiral Jokic, the one that he gave the OTP investigators?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember explicitly citing -- indicating this. I would have to look at it. Explicitly -- I do not recall explicitly mentioning any of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I be allowed to remind you, for example: In your report, there is a section referring to Admiral Jokic allegedly requesting the removal of some of the commanders. Does that jog your memory?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I do remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your report, did you include that information only after you had studied the interview that Admiral Jokic had given to the OTP investigators?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember correctly - I do not know my report by heart - I only used the fact that his proposals for replacement of individual senior officers were not adopted. However, I did not really mention any fact to prove it, and therefore, I did not even cite it as a source of my report. But by way of explanation, perhaps this fact was used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, sir: Did you perhaps see two different interviews that Admiral Jokic gave to the OTP investigators?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that there were two interviews. I only looked at one such set. Whether it was composed of one part, two parts, I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the interview you said you saw? Do you know what the date is of that interview? Was this interview conducted in July 2002 or in September 2003?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that was that second interview.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: September 2003, then; right?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you not indicate in one of the footnotes that you had used that particular interview? Because you did indicate other information. You indicated your sources, and this was one of the sources you used for information, and you used this information in your report, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think having referred anywhere directly to this interview and have not quoted anything from this interview [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. We'll get back to that later on. Sir, in your report, do you speak about the attack against Dubrovnik by the JNA or do you address this matter in a different way?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if anywhere I did assess the kind of such activity, I used -- probably used the term "blockade" or perhaps "the attack," possibly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is a difference, isn't there, between blockade and attack, in military, technical terms?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... of attack or a form of attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: The JNA maps that you looked at, were there any markings or symbols to indicate that the situation facing Dubrovnik was that of an attack?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, this on the map was not the decision to attack, and signs reflecting an attack activity, this was not indicated, but only the deployment of the forces in the blockade of this area, and also outside the Dubrovnik area. Therefore, deployment of the forces -- of units, units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If what was being shown on those maps was an attack, would there not be arrows on the map showing the axis of attack taken by JNA units?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this map contained a decision for attack, that would be so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, in your report, you distinguish between three different kinds of operational groups. Those are your words. Sir, the 2nd Operational Group, which category of operational groups would it belong to? After all, your report is in relation to the 2nd Operational Group, and you have studied the relevant documents, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't spoken of types of operational groups. Well, it is possible to form operational -- other operational groups as such. At that time, I dealt with -- the fact that at that time I didn't know and today I also do not know exactly who exactly formed or set up the 2nd Operational Group, that I established, after identifying its composition, that, in view of this composition, such a group, and in view of its tasks, such a group could belong to the group established by the General Staff, and I've mentioned that version, or that option, as the last or the third in the row.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, sir: The 2nd Operational Group, was it in any way peculiar in terms of the composition of its branches?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I myself cannot see any specific features. If the group is set up by the General Staff, and the fact that in its composition it involves the naval sector together with corps of the ground forces doesn't seem anything special to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the composition of the 2nd Operational Group as on the 1st of October, 1991? What did it consist of?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can remember, in particular, from the working map, that the operational group, in its make-up, in its composition, involved 37th Corps of the ground forces, 2nd Corps of the ground forces, and the 9th Military Naval Sector. Whether and which or what other independent units fell within the framework of its composition, I do not know. For my assessment, the structure on the level of corps was sufficient.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, when was the 2nd Tactical Group established?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what the task was, the objective of the 2nd Tactical Group, as part of the 2nd Operational Group? I assume, then, you're not familiar with the composition of the 2nd Tactical Group either, are you? Do you know when the Prevlaka Combat Group was set up? Then you probably know nothing about its composition or its tasks, do you? Sir, do you know anything about the manoeuvres of the 472nd Motorised Brigade between the 1st of October and the 31st of December, 1991? My apologies. Sir, I was talking about the period between the 1st of October and the 31st of December, 1991. Were you familiar with the whereabouts and the manoeuvres of that brigade as part of its -- of the operational group?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All movements?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. No. Establishment-wise, how the brigade moved, as part of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the combat organisation.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know what you have in mind with formation movement, but I assume you have in mind to whom at that time it was subordinate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exit and entry, the independent nature of that unit in the period of time given, 1st of October to 31st of December?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, actually, in my report I didn't deal with this issue, but from documentation, I can recall that all the time it was part of the 2nd Operational Group. Its parts were subordinate to different commands, and from battalions, perhaps temporarily too, were subordinate to the 9th VPS, Military Naval Sector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. My apologies. One of my previous questions in relation to the setting up, composition and tasks of the Prevlaka Combat Group that was part of the 2nd Operational Group at the time, the transcript does not reflect the answer you gave. You said you knew nothing about that, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that a convenient time, Mr. Rodic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is, indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Then we will take the first morning break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have been asked by the interpretation team to take into account the technical possibilities that exist; namely, two booths cannot be working on the same channel at the same time. So I have to ask you, Mr. Zorc, to please pause for my question to end and for its interpretation to end, because my question is being interpreted into English and into Slovenian, and then your answer is interpreted. So we have several of your short answers missing from the transcript. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the break, I asked you about the interview of Admiral Jokic, that you say that you studied but you do not remember whether you referred to it at all in your report. I would ask you kindly to look at page 23. It's page 23 of the report in B/C/S. That's the version I have. But it is the section that has to do with military discipline, section 5. So it is the answer that you give to the question in subparagraph (a). In the last paragraph of your question under (a), you say in the documentary material, except for the document that has to do with the interview with Vice Admiral Jokic, I did not find a single document which would prove that other more effective measures were taken. For example, disciplinary measures, filing of criminal complaints and personnel charges. Even his proposals of staff changes that pertain to certain commanding officers had not been accepted. Does that mean that you believe what you read in that interview? And let me help you. It is in page 26 of the Slovenian version of the report, the third paragraph starting from the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right. The only document from which I could see that his proposals had not been accepted, I've seen that in his interview. But I would like to correct you. I had not studied his interview. I only went rapidly -- browsed through it, because I noticed no source of information for the questions that I had been given.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, as for these changes that were not effected, you take that from the interview and you take it as a fact, you take it at face value?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also, on page 21 of your report, that is, subparagraph (g), so the answer to the question under subparagraph (g) -- sorry. It is (h). I'm actually referring to (h). Again, I'm looking at the last paragraph of your answer. You say: "From the interview with Vice Admiral Miodrag Jokic, one can note that the commander of the 2nd operative group [as interpreted] had frequent contact with the commander of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade and that officers from his command were stationed in this battalion." Do you also take this as a fact upon which you base your findings, and it is actually contained in Admiral Jokic's interview to the OTP in September 2003?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why, then, did you not mention this interview with Admiral Jokic in the footnotes of the material that you used, since you treat these facts as significant ones and you base some of your findings in the report on them? Was this omitted by accident, by mistake?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe. It may -- you may consider it a mistake, but in my text, I did mention from where I had this view. I felt no need to have also a footnote on it. And I mentioned it, that it was the interview with Admiral Jokic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, these two questions I mentioned to you just now, since they were taken from the interview with Admiral Jokic, you consider them to be relevant for your report because you base your opinion on them; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether you know in whose organisational and establishment units the 472nd Motorised Brigade from Trebinje was before these combat activities started and these actions taken by the 2nd Operational Group?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far -- the organisation of the JNA was known to me prior to 1991, this brigade was an integral part of the 9th VPS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to ask that the witness be shown P133. That is from Admiral Jokic's binder. It is tab 41. I would like to ask you, Mr. Zorc, to look at 03390470, please. It is the page that follows Captain Kovacevic's active service. Under these first two items, do you see that Kovacevic was at the reserve officer's school in Bileca, that he served there?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under the next item, do you see that the order issued by the personnel department of the Federal Secretariat for National Defence, dated the 27th of July, 1989, he is transferred to the Trebinje garrison of the Military Naval District? That is the third item from the top of the page. That's the one that refers to -- or rather, the fifth one. I'm sorry. Or sixth, rather. He is transferred from the garrison due to the needs of the service, to the Trebinje garrison.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at the third item further down. Acting commander of the 3rd Motorised Company of the 3rd Motorised Battalion. And then it says under the column "unit or institution," it says: "The 472nd Motorised Brigade, 'R' 9th VPS, 'A' under quotation marks, VPO." That is the military naval district, the Trebinje garrison.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that confirm -- is that confirmed, rather, by these official documents, that is, that what you knew before 1991, that the 472nd Motorised Brigade, from the point of view of organisation, its establishment is within the 9th VPS or rather military naval district?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I will no longer be needing this document. I would like to ask that the witness be shown a Defence exhibit, D43, please. Mr. Zorc, tell me, please: Did you have the opportunity of seeing this document earlier on when you were studying the materials for this?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is an order of the command of the 2nd Operational Group dated the 25th of October concerning the return of the 472nd Motorised Brigade to their original establishment; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm for us one's own establishment, one's own unit, does that mean that the brigade returns to its own command, or rather, the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. organisation and establishment that it belongs to, namely, the 9th VPS, that it belonged to earlier on?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I won't be needing the document any more. If, from the 9th Military Naval Sector, by order of the appropriate command, a unit -- or rather, the 472nd Motorised Brigade is temporarily relocated and re-subordinated to a different command, is that brigade still, from the point of view of organisation and establishment, within the 9th Military Naval Sector, but it is temporarily re-subordinated or attached elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This means that its parent command is the 9th VPS, but that for the use of that unit, another command has the competence for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As for the documents that you studied, could you follow the 472nd Brigade in the period from the 1st of October until the 31st of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not deal especially with that issue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see in which period the entire brigade, the entire 472nd Brigade, was under the command of the 9th Military Naval Sector?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the document which you have just showed me, if I remember correctly, there was a date, the 25th of October, 1991. This is what I have seen just now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While studying this documentation, did you see when only individual battalions of this brigade were directly subordinated to the command of the 9th Military Naval Sector?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The exact time of the re-subordination of the individual battalions was not in my interest, and I don't know that. But I was interested and determined was that [as interpreted] the 3rd Battalion was at a certain period of time, in December, was subordinated to the command of the 9th VPS, while the brigade was not under the subordination of the 9th. It was under the direct command of the 2nd Operational Group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you mentioned the 3rd Battalion, you mentioned the subordination of the 472nd Brigade to the 9th VPS in December 1991? Is that what you meant?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned in your report, when speaking of the 6th of December and the incident which was allegedly caused by the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade, could you establish on the basis of relevant documents under whose command the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade was at the time and who it was directly subordinated to?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I remember, the 3rd Battalion at the time was subordinated directly to the command of the 9th VPS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you perhaps know about the rest of the 472nd Motorised Brigade? There were three battalions left there. Among whose temporary units were they at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were a part of the 2nd Operational Group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which corps?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall in the documentation and at the time at my disposal that this brigade would have been subordinated to some other corps. As I understood, it was under the direct command of the 2nd Operational Group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: The operative objective of the 2nd Operational Group, in connection with the town of Dubrovnik itself, was it the blockade of the town of Dubrovnik? Was that the operative objective?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of your question, as an introduction, I must inform Your Honours that in my expert report, I did not go into these professional issues, as far as tasks and manner of combat operations of the 2nd Operational Group. But from a certain document, the command of the naval military district, I saw that the task, the operational task, was the blockade of Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, it is the order of the command of the military naval district, the order to use forces of the VPO dated the 20th of September, 1991. Is that the document that you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be of assistance if you could be shown this document? It is in tab 12, P199.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The binder of General Zorc, tab 12, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zorc, can I help you? If you meant this document under number 2, task of the VPO, that's on page 1, and then the second paragraph: "Units of the 9th VPS of the 472nd Motorised Brigade to break out on the Adriatic highway in the wider area of Dubrovnik as soon as possible, lift the blockade of the Kupari military resort, seize control of the Srdj installation, impose a blockade on the city of Dubrovnik and cut it off from the rest of the territory of the Republic of Croatia." Is that the document?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look further on, item 3, or rather, item 4 -- I'm sorry, in page 2, in paragraph 2, it says: "Use part of the forces of the 472nd Motorised Brigade to break out on to the Adriatic highway in the wider sector of Dubrovnik, lift the blockade of military installations, impose a blockade on the city of Dubrovnik and cut it off from the rest of the territory of the Republic of Croatia." Can that be interpreted as the operational objective of the military naval district?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This could not be an operational objective of the VPO. This is the idea of the commander of VPO, on the basis of which he decided that, with a part of the forces, he blocks Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct -- since you say that that is the underlying idea of this document, this document is entitled "Order to use the forces of the military naval district operative number 1."

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In item 2, we see that this is the task of the military naval district and its units; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As regards Dubrovnik and the blockade of Dubrovnik, according to this order, is it true that this task pertains to the units of the 9th Military Naval Sector and the 472nd Brigade within that sector?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no. There is a general decision of that commander and which states that he decided that the task of blockading Dubrovnik, he will perform with a part of his forces. It means the 472nd Motorised Brigade. It does not speak in any way of the 9th VPS. This is not a task. It's the decision concerning this brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, in paragraph 2, it says: "Units of the 9th VPS," and in parentheses: "[The 472nd Motorised Brigade]."

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But this is the task that was entrusted to the commander from the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall no longer be needing this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also, in response to the question put to you by my learned friend of the Prosecution, you said that you had the opportunity of seeing a draft directive, a draft decision for the attack operation that the command of the 2nd Operational Group, on the 29th of September, 1991, submitted to the chief of General Staff of the armed forces, to Lieutenant Colonel General [as interpreted] Blagoje Adzic.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that document, could you see the operational objectives of the 2nd Operational Group, or rather, its task in its entirety?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, the content of this document is the complete decision of the 2nd Operational Group. Prior to issuing the order, it was sent to the General Staff for approval. But I would have to look into it now in order to see exactly what it contains.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, excuse me. Is it possible for the witness to have the document in front of him?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is precisely what I wish to suggest right now. It is D44.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you receive this other document, and when we were discussing the previous order of the military naval district dated the 20th of September, 1991, could it be seen from that order that the 9th Military Naval Sector at that point in time, together with the 472nd Motorised Brigade, was within the military naval district? That pertains to the previous document that you looked at.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. I think it's quite the opposite. I believe that the 9th VPS, in that order, did not receive a concrete task, concrete assignment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was it within the military naval district at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This would more probably mean that it was not in this district at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the 472nd Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That brigade probably was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please look at this draft decision for the attack operation that the command of the 2nd Operational Group submitted to the chief of General Staff for his approval. If you look at item 1 of this draft decision for the attack operation, can you see the tasks listed there for the 2nd Operational Group, as well as their objectives?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Here, you can see the ideological part of the decision of the commander of the 2nd Operational Group. However, this part of the decision always corresponds to the task that was given to the 2nd Operational Group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did the 2nd Operational Group get such an order from?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the fact who was given this decision for approval, it is evident that the subordinated commander was the chief staff of the Armed Forces of Yugoslavia [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. The transcript reflects -- excuse me. The transcript said it is evident that the subordinated commander was the chief of staff [sic]. And I would ask if counsel could inquire if it was meant superior commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is correct. You were a bit faster than I was, and I was about to correct that, to set the record straight. There was an error, and my question was: Who did the 2nd Operational Group get this order from? You said, or at least that was the interpretation I got, from the subordinated Chief of Staff. So can you please run the question by me again.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. They got it from the superior, that is, the General Staff. And if the mistake is mine, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. While studying the documentation, were you in a position to obtain information as to who had established the 2nd Operational Group?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before I could see the document that you have just shown to me, I could only conclude, and I concluded from the size and the structure of the 2nd Operational Group, which is composed of the corps of different military districts, and that showed to me that the 2nd Operational Group could only be established by the General Staff. From the document I have here now, this is unequivocally, in fact, demonstrated, confirmed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Can you please now have a look at item 1. In this draft decision for the attack operation, is there any reference to the need to carry out the blockade from both sea and land in Dubrovnik, the Cilipi airport as well as the Prevlaka area?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there anything else you can tell us about the objectives of the 2nd Operational Group, based on this draft decision? Do you see any other objectives listed there?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The 2nd Operational Group evidently had a broader task to perform than just the blockade of Dubrovnik. It had to intersect the links of Dubrovnik, the connections of the Dubrovnik [as interpreted], with the central part of the coast, or, in other words, the Republic of Croatia. It had to isolate the Cilipi airport, Dubrovnik, and also, in fact, make impossible a manoeuvre by the opposing forces against the blocked parts, blockaded parts of the coast. On the other hand, the 2nd Operational Group had to, in fact, secure the part in the central parts and in fact the area around Mostar. Later on, in further combat -- in further activities, it had to be prepared already after the performance of such tasks be ready, therefore, for combat activities on the right side of Neretva; therefore, western Herzegovina. So that is one thing I can establish. And the second is, and that is related to the question as to the differentiation between a blockade or attack, well, on the basis of this document, I can point out that this document is a directive for attack and that the blockade of Dubrovnik is part of this attack, as I have explained in my answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, sir: The 37th Corps, or the 2nd Operational Group, were they involved in the Mostar area, in the Mostar airport area, more specifically?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The 37th Corps in given set-up formation was a part of the 2nd Operational Group and was active in the Neretva Valley and in the Mostar area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you were commander of the 4th Sarajevo Corps back in 1991, weren't you? What about the 10th Motorised Brigade from Mostar? Was it within the composition of your corps?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether that brigade too, the Mostar Brigade, was part of the 2nd Operational Group once this was set up?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the documents here in my hands, I can see that for this operation, the 10th Motorised Brigade of the 4th Corps was re-subordinated to the 37th Corps of the land forces, which was within the composition of the 2nd Operational Group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We'll no longer be needing this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who the commanders were of the 2nd Operational Group between the 1st of October and the 31st of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know it from documents, but I know it from general information I have. I think that before admiral -- before General Strugar, the commander of this group was General Ruzinovski, but I don't know for sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about before General Ruzinovski?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that since the 3rd Operational Group was set up, there were three commanders there? 2nd Operational Group, I'm sorry. My mistake.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think that is so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the respective time periods in relation to the 1st of October and the 31st of December, 1991, in terms of when those respective commanders were removed?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
