utterances.text: If there was a quick succession of three different commanders in a unit that was as big -- and, quite importantly, this was a provisional, temporary unit or formation -- would that have any sort of influence on the issues that you reviewed in your report, from the standpoint of command and control problems?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In formal terms, that should not have an influence on the activities of the 2nd Operational Group. In fact, however, any change of commanding officer does influence the activities, the functioning of the operational group, and ultimately the removal or replacement of the commanders of the 2nd Operational Group did not have an influence, influence that you are asking me about, at the point of time for which you asked me about the responsibilities and obligations of the commander of the 2nd Operational Group. Because the period that was interesting for my answers, in fact, at that time there was only one commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In your report, in B/C/S, the pages 7, chapter 1 -- rather, chapter 2, command and control, this is item C of your report. The second-last paragraph of your answer, the third case would be if the General Staff were to form an operational group from the different military districts. Have you found that? In that passage, you say: "If the General Staff were to form this unit from different -- several different military districts, this operational group would be commanded and controlled by the relevant general and the staff from the units making up that group." Can you perhaps shed some light on this. What exactly would that mean?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if in the case that the General Staff forms an operational group, they -- he -- it has to appoint the commander of the operational group and also entrust it with the command of the operational group, and that is demanding, a demanding project in terms of staffing, because you have to take these officers from somewhere. In regular practice and in normal practice, it would be regular that -- it would usually be that in fact an officer can be appointed also from its composition. However, the other and the majority of officers almost necessarily have to be found in the command composition of the units that are part of the operational group. However, it should be done by making sure that the functioning of the command of units, participating units, not be made impossible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While studying the documentation, did you perhaps come across the following fact, namely, that the setting up of the command of the 2nd Operational Group, as well as later on the staff of that very command, were made up predominantly by officers from the general inspection unit from Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps come across any document indicating that officers from the general inspection unit, the Belgrade-based one, were temporarily sent to work with the 2nd Operational Group?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's something else -- I don't remember that either. In view of the fact that General Ruzinovski, in a point in time, was inspector general and that he was the commander of the 2nd Operational Group in a period, but that's a period before. That was not the object of my interest. This is -- it is from this that I make my assumption.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please have a look now at the next passage of your answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the last passage, you say the following: You speak about an order received from a superior command to set up an operational group, and this order should contain command authorisation; isn't that the case? Further on, it says if this authorisation is limited in any way, if the powers are limited in any way, and in parenthesis, for example, only limited to operational leadership decisions on engaging units, this should be clearly stated in the order. While drafting your report, did you have a chance to, in terms of commanding powers, to base your position on a document that you had studied?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the entire answer in my report to this question, it is apparent that I did not have before me, and I did not see, the order of the General Staff whereby the 2nd Operational Group was established. Hence, all these possibilities of the establishment of the unit stated here in this paragraph, including the last paragraph, I wrote as something probable and possible. Therefore, how -- what should be done and how it should be done. But I could not really say how this was done, and I think that the way this is formulated shows it. Therefore, it is in the conditional, "would be."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, sir, in view of the fact that you never saw such a document, you can't say with any degree of certainty what the commanding powers would be in a specific case, can you?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, when we talk about a temporary military formation, such as the 2nd Operational Group, in your report, you refer to the rules on the authority of the corps command of the land forces in peacetime. This is at tab 8. And the exhibit number is P196.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have the usher's assistance, please. I would like to show the witness this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have the document in front of you, sir? Can you please look at Article 6 of the rules. In paragraph 1, the following is stated: "The right to command units and institutions of the organic compound of KOV, land army corps, hereinafter corps, is under the exclusive responsibility of the commander. Units and institutions outside the corps, the corps's organic compound, those temporarily subordinated are commanded and controlled by the commander only within the limits of the stipulated authorities or powers." What about this second sentence? Is that a reference to the command authority in relation to temporarily re-subordinated units?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that in compliance with my previous question in relation to the command authority of the 2nd Operational Group, or rather, the commander of the 2nd Operational Group?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And precisely because this second sentence of Article 6, which is written here for the corps but is still, in fact, generally applicable in the military organisation. Having known that and not having had a document stipulating precisely these authorities, these powers, I, in fact, drew attention to this in my report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, sir: Do you know that the 9th Military Naval Sector had naval forces and coastal defence forces, that in the period between the 1st of October and the 31st of December, 1991, were in fact subordinated to the command of the military naval district and not to the 2nd Operational Group? May I just give you an example. I'm not sure if you're familiar with the Lustica Peninsula and the coastal defence there. It's a division with patrol boats. Military sabotage units.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: That is making reference to a fact that is not in evidence. It has never been proven.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is this a matter which will be the subject of evidence, Mr. Rodic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You clearly can postulate what you intend to establish, if that's relevant to getting a comment or an answer from the witness, but you don't -- not yet in a position to put it as an established fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fair enough. I'll try to reword my question, in that case, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I'll put it to the witness in the form of a hypothesis. Mr. Zorc, if within its composition the 9th VPS also had other units, units that were not used as part of the operational group, such as, for example, the coastal defence unit at the Lustica Peninsula, the patrol boat division, the naval sabotage detachment, the naval infantry brigade based in Bar, what about those elements of the 9th VPS? Through the VPS, would they not be under the competence of the military naval district, under their authority, in that period of time?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This would only be the case if, to the 9th Military Naval Sector, these -- the units mentioned would be removed from under its authority and kept under the command of the district of the military naval district. If this was not done, these units remained under the authority of its regular command, therefore, the command of the 9th VPS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe in answer to one of my previous questions you made reference to territorial jurisdiction, or rather, area of responsibility of the 9th VPS. Do you know if that area of responsibility of the 9th VPS stretched between Ploce and Otranto in the south Adriatic?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the north, I think you are right. It was from Ploce. In the south, it's accurate to the border of Yugoslavia, as far as the border of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, based on documents related to the 2nd Operational Group, were you able to draw any conclusions or to see, actually, that the command of the 2nd Operational Group was taking into account, or rather, that the land between Montenegro's borders, the Croatian-Montenegrin border and the Albanian border was actually part of their responsibility? What about that bit of territory under the 9th VPS area of responsibility? Was that under the 2nd Operational Group too?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the documents that I could see, I in fact could not see that in fact the scope of responsibility of the 2nd Operational Group would be accurately defined. And in these documents, again of the 2nd Operational Group, I could not find, for instance, any indication that the 2nd Operational Group was given any task for the area to the south of Boka Kotorska to the Albanian border.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are now talking about the area of responsibility of the 9th VPS. What would normally be its area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, given that you spent a portion of 1991 with the JNA, do you know if after you left the JNA, and around that time, or rather, when exactly in 1991 was it that units of the navy were moved from the Adriatic section of the coast, and here I'm referring to Slovenia, down through Croatia towards Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I have noted while still being in active military service, no such movements took place. That was until June 1991. At least I wasn't notified of any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where the navy units and equipment were moved to, when they were moved from Croatian territory?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In time, while I still was in active military service, I have no idea of such movements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about late 1991?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Following the beginning of conflicts on the soil of Slovenia and Croatia, of course, certain manoeuvres did take place, and the forces of VPO D, VPO [as interpreted], did make a manoeuvring towards the south.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about those navy forces? Were they moved alongside with all of their equipment to Montenegro, or rather, moved into the area of responsibility of the 9th VPS?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know of that accurately, but with part of the forces, most probably, they were moved to individual islands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Sir, as a high-ranking officer, you must be familiar with the content and the manner in which military documents are drafted, such as regular combat reports and orders for attack. Can you please briefly tell us about what the elements of those documents are.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, combat order for attack contains the following essential integral parts. The first item, a brief information on how the command issuing order assesses the operation or the activities of the opposite side must be conveyed. In the second item, the task that the command was vested from the superior command should be conveyed. And in the third item, the data are conveyed according to which the tasks are performed with the neighbouring units, concerning the activities we're talking about. The fourth item contains the decision taken by the commander as to the ways and means he had in mind to be able to carry out the task stemming from item 2, received from superior command. Furthermore, the conceptual part of this issue is conveyed in the following item, and in the following items, the competent commander issuing this particular order determines the tasks of all his subordinate units taking part in the implementation of the task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I apologise for interrupting you, but this is quite enough for my purposes. Could you just briefly tell me: Regular combat reports forwarded by a commander of a unit to its own superior command, does that sort of report also contain information on the enemy and their operations?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This also, since the intelligence functions, is also a function of all the subordinate units. The data that they receive in the direct contact or conflict with the enemy, they convey forwards, both in the form of the report and beyond this form, while they're getting this information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me: In the regular combat report, this information about the enemy I assume contain a summary of the most relevant information that the subordinate units can provide to their command about the enemy, or information that is collected through intelligence sources?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a general synthesis of the data that the report contains and that command then rounds up and conveys to the superior command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please: If we have the example of an order for attack, when in the first paragraph information about the enemy is provided, is the purpose of this information to caution one's own units of enemy forces and possible dangers coming from those forces, dangers that may happen or that they may encounter in combat activity?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, the purpose of this item is to inform the subordinate units on wider activities of the enemy, whether a specific deployment, and with the assessment that the command issuing orders has, on purposes and capabilities of the enemy in the time expected. This is an essential piece of information for subordinate commanders, enabling them correctly -- to correctly understand the order given by the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown D57, Defence Exhibit D57. Could the English translation of this document please be placed on the overhead projector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zorc, this is a document that was admitted into evidence during this trial. It is an order for attack of the command of the 9th Military Naval Sector dated the 9th of November, 1991. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm interested in the following now: In view of your previous answers, in paragraph 1, information is given about the enemy; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at the third sentence in that document, where it says: "From the fortresses of the Old Town centre, he is using mobile mortars, 82-millimetres and 60-millimetres." The command of the 9th VPS, including the commander, who signed this order for attack, does the command in this way inform its subordinate units about the whereabouts of the enemy and about the locations from which they would possibly be in danger?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, evidently.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the usher now to give the witness the following exhibits: D58 and D62. Thank you. We won't be needing this document any longer. I would also like to ask for the English translation to be placed on the ELMO again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zorc, do you have before you document D58, which is a regular combat report of the command of the 9th Military Naval Sector dated the 10th of November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please take a look at paragraph 1 again. It is entitled "The Enemy." In the second paragraph of paragraph 1, it says, towards the end, that the enemy still uses the hotel resorts in the walls of the Old Town for mortar positions. Is that what it says there?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this information now of the 9th Military Naval Sector to their superior command, the 2nd Operational Group, about enemy positions and operations?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask you to look at the other document now, D62.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, this is a regular combat report of the 9th Military Naval Sector dated the 6th of December, 1991. It was sent to the command of the 2nd Operational Group. Can you see in paragraph 1 that pertains to the enemy yet again, in the third paragraph, it says the enemy kept changing the positions of the mortars so that fire was occasionally opened from the Stradun area, as well as from the Old City port?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that also consist of information provided by the 9th Military Naval Sector to their superior command on the enemy dated the 6th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was written from 1700 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We will no longer be needing these documents. You can put them back. Mr. Zorc, could you please tell us the following: You were commander of a division, commander of a corps. As corps commander in Sarajevo, did you have three or four brigades subordinated to you within that corps?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether it's three or four.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you interested in the number?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm going to put a hypothetical question to you. Let us mark them as the first, second and third Brigade. The commander of a battalion in the first brigade committed a disciplinary infraction, because of which he is supposed to come and report to you. The reason why is not important. But is there a reason why the commander of the first battalion from the first brigade should come to report to you? Do you call in his immediate superior officer then at the same time so that he could hear about all of this and see what it was all about? Did this happen in practice?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In case I wanted to get a battalion commander to report to me, in every case, I would ask that he be brought to me by the commander of the brigade, even though this could have been a completely exceptional situation because the report is given by the first superior commander, normally commander of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's precisely what I'm asking about. I'm asking about an exceptional situation. You say that in that case, by all means you would call his immediate superior, the commander of the brigade, so that he would be present too; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In case you call in for a report, the commander of the brigade, would this reporting in any case be attended by any of the subordinates of that brigade commander, for example, a battalion commander?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not possible at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: In this first solution that we discussed, that you call the battalion commander to report to you, and then his immediate superior officer comes in with him, the brigade commander, in that way, do you want at the same time for the first -- the immediate superior officer of the battalion commander, and that is, the brigade commander, to hear during the reporting the reasons why the battalion commander has been asked to come in, and also that he familiarise himself with possible tasks, orders, or decisions that you would adopt after that?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In relation to that, can I just ask you one more thing? Is that something that was in JNA doctrine and practice? Was that the way it always was during practice in JNA service, not only in your particular case but in the JNA, the Yugoslav People's Army, in general?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Regular report is given by the immediate superior commander. If the next superior commander wishes to have a talk with the second superior commander, it's called conversation, not report. Because report is already an expression for the implementation of disciplinary responsibility, and it is the immediate superior commander that is giving the report, although superior commanders are not excluded and have possibility to take action.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When I asked you about this, we established that already a while ago when we are talking about exceptional situations, when you have a problem of such a nature that you, as corps commander, found it necessary to call in for a report a battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If the situation were as exceptional as this, I would no doubt demand that the brigade commander brings them in, unless there were some other reasons indicating that this would not be fitting or appropriate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In any case, when the situation is an exceptional one, the higher level of command -- or let me withdraw this question and let me try to make it as specific as possible. So, is it certain that a brigade commander, in relation to a problem for which he has been asked to come in for a report, would not appear before a corps commander in the presence of one of his subordinates, like a battalion commander, and the superior officer would never be criticised before his subordinate?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, would this be an appropriate time to take a break now? Because I would like to move on to a different topic now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well, then, Mr. Rodic. We'll take our second break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Can the witness please be shown Defence Exhibit D50. May the English copy please be displayed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Zorc, is it true, based on this document, that the deputy federal secretary, Admiral Stane Brovet, is requesting to have information forwarded urgently regarding the allegations from the protest of the international monitoring mission, dated the 3rd of November, 1991, and that this request was first of all sent to the commander of the 9th VPS, Miodrag Jokic, and secondly to the commander of the 2nd Operational Group, Colonel General Pavle Strugar?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The deputy federal secretary, by virtue of his official position, does he belong to a higher command than the command of the 2nd Operational Group? What would be the rank in terms of command?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is a higher rank than the 2nd Operational Group. Deputy federal secretary, he is the level, the rank, of the federal secretary for national defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this specific case, he, as deputy federal secretary, is asking at the same time both from the commander of the 2nd Operational Group and from his subordinate commander to clarify this problem that he is writing to them about?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't a normal situation, but it's obvious that he urgently needed this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not receiving interpretation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'm again receiving interpretation now. Are there exceptional situations, urgent situations, or particularly important situations, where the highest, or rather, very high level of command and control may address a person or a command such as the 9th VPS, which is, in terms of subordination, in terms of the chain of command, below the 2nd Operational Group, with a direct request for information from them?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is indeed possible. And the question which was raised was obviously in the authority of the deputy federal secretary, and it's also obvious that it was urgent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would this kind of situation in the specific case, can the federal secretary address the commander of the 9th VPS only if he sees it fit and believes that he is the best potential source of information on what he wants to know?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It would be possible to get the best -- not only the best information, but also the fastest. But he acted correctly by sending also this request to the commander of the 2nd Operational Group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness now please be shown Exhibit P104. OTP Exhibit P104.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Zorc, sir, can you tell me, please, once you've looked at the document P104, the Prosecution exhibit, is that General Strugar's response, in his capacity as commander of the 2nd Operational Group, to a request made by the deputy federal secretary, Admiral Brovet, in relation to the protest filed by the ECMM, and Admiral Brovet requested an urgent response?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of the document that I have in my hands now, it's clear that it was sent to the deputy of the federal secretary, Admiral Stane Brovet. It's a report which was sent in on the same day. They received the request for a report on this issue, and in the contents of this report, they inform the deputy national secretary about the matter he had inquired about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll no longer be needing that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness now please be shown Defence Exhibit D51.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Zorc, sir, is this the reply sent by the command of the 9th VPS and Admiral Jokic to the deputy federal secretary for national defence, Admiral Brovet, containing a report on the problem under consideration, the problem spoken about by Mr. Brovet in D50, the document that you just looked at?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document that I have in front of me was a handwritten document, and whether this is the handwriting of the Admiral Jokic, the commander of the 9th VPS, it is a report sent in on the 4th of November and which was also directly sent to the deputy federal secretary and to the 2nd Operational Group. It was also submitted for their knowledge. And prior to that, we saw also the report sent in by the 2nd Operational Group concerning the same issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just for the sake of the transcript: The document was sent directly to the federal secretary, or rather, his deputy, and to the attention of the 2nd Operational Group. That is indeed reflected in the transcript, but not with sufficient clarity. Therefore, I believe it's necessary to point it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll try to get the matter clarified through further questions. When the commander of the 9th VPS sends his reply directly to the deputy federal secretary, as another addressee, he also indicates the command of the 2nd Operational Group, and he sends this report to the attention of the command of the 2nd Operational Group. Would that mean that Admiral Jokic, as General Strugar's subordinate, wishes hereby to inform him about what he had previously reported to Admiral Brovet following the assignment that he had previously received from Admiral Brovet himself?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, that was the purpose of sending it also "to the attention of."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We are done with that document for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness now please be shown Defence Exhibit D65.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, just a point of objection. Counsel, I believe, in the last question to the witness gave it an interpretation instead of making it a clear question, where he said "previously sending," and it's not clear whether it's previously sending to Admiral Brovet or simultaneously. That is purely counsel's speculative interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if necessary, I can get the matter clarified with the witness again, if there's something left unclear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Zorc, in relation to -- General Zorc, sir, in relation to this last document, you saw that it was marked by General Jokic [as interpreted] as addressed to the deputy federal secretary, and just underneath it said to the command of the 2nd Operational Group, rather, to the attention of the command of the 2nd Operational Group. As the document was sent to the deputy federal secretary, in terms of its substance, was that a direct reply to the deputy federal secretary following his own request contained in the first document, to be especially informed, to receive special reports by the commander of the VPS and the commander of the 2nd Operational Group, both?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. The commander of the 9th VPS sent his reply directly to Admiral Brovet because also Admiral Brovet directly sent that request to him. But he was aware that he must also inform his superior, so that he -- the superior commander is fully aware of the situation and what has been sent as a reply to Admiral Brovet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I may be about to ask you a question that might strike you as not completely logical, but I must run this past you again to get the matter clarified. When Admiral Brovet looked at that document, had he just received a report from Vice Admiral Jokic --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Objection. Speculative, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe this is no speculation. General Zorc is an OTP expert. He's a military expert with a lot of experience in the area. He's here to provide his expert opinion. He's here to provide his expert interpretation of the military documents that are placed in front of him. These military documents bear a seal, and they have been admitted into evidence during the course of this very trial. And also, we know exactly when the document was sent. There's an outgoing stamp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think it is the timing of the two documents that is the point of concern of the objection. I am not altogether clear about the point of the objection, but I am certainly clear that you, in your questions, are assuming an order of reading of them by Admiral Brovet, and I don't know that there is any basis for you to assume that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. Maybe there has been a slight misunderstanding, or perhaps my question was slightly confusing. That was not my intention, however. I'll try to get this clarified now. So it's quite irrelevant, immaterial to me which was the first report read by Admiral Brovet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I want to know is the following, General Zorc, sir, if we can just go back to my previous question. I'm talking about document D51, which is the report by Admiral Jokic, commander of the 9th VPS, the report that he sent to Admiral Brovet. That document, that report, there's a second title, or the addressee, in a manner of speaking, to the attention of the 2nd Operational Group. Now, my question is: Does that mean that Admiral Jokic wanted to also submit this report that he had sent to Admiral Brovet to his own superior, the commander of the 2nd Operational Group, so that he would be informed with the substance of this report, the same report that reached Admiral Brovet?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, precisely for that reason he sent this report to the attention of.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honour, I believe the matter is now sufficiently clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think that part was clear from the outset. The concern, I think, was one that arose from the form of your questions. You were not conscious of other implications in your questions, and Ms. Somers was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us move on, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Zorc, sir, you have in front of you D65. Can you please tell us what document this is. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my hands I have a report of the command of the 9th Military Naval Sector dated 7th of December, 1991, on the action of the 3rd Battalion, 472nd Motorised Brigade, on Srdj, on the 6th of December, 1991. The report has been sent by the 9th Military Naval Sector command to the First Administration of the General Staff, to General Simonovic. And here we have a description concerning actions on Srdj on the 6th, and in the introduction, additional data concerning two officers, the captain, the commander of that brigade, and the head of the staff of the 5th Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fair enough. General Zorc, who signed this document? Who sent this document out? Whose document is it?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was signed by Vice Admiral Miodrag Jokic. That's the name that is here only typed out, but I do not see any signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, sir: This addressee, the First Administration for General Simonovic, is this an operative administration within the General Staff of the Armed Forces of the SFRY?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This report was sent to the First Administration, the operational administration, and it's -- first we have the basic information on commanders of the units which participated in the action.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, sir: Based on this document, does it indicate or could it lead you to assume that the document was also submitted or forwarded to the commander of the 2nd Operational Group, as we have seen with the previous document, in the case of Admiral Brovet, where it said to the attention of the 2nd OG? Does this document seem to indicate anything like that?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In this document, one cannot conclude that it had been also sent to the commander of the 2nd Operational Group. It's not indicated either here at the heading after the main addressee, nor is it indicated later, below the signature, that it had been submitted also to the commander of the 2nd organisational [as interpreted] group. So it is a report which has been exclusively sent to the two levels -- two -- superior officer, two levels above.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. Just briefly, please: When you drafted your report, your expert opinion, did you take that document into account? Did you review the document back then?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have it here in front of me for the first time now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown OTP document P61, tab 39. This is from the Hvalkof binder, if I'm not mistaken. My apologies. I believe I've given you the wrong reference. My apologies, Your Honours. There seems to have been a little confusion. Let me just check the document number again. If my learned friend and colleague could just give me a hand with this, please. This is a report by Admiral Jokic dated the 9th of December. This report was sent to the deputy federal secretary, Admiral Brovet.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that counsel was correct in his first tab. It was P61, tab 39. If this is the damage report. Is that what -- if I may inquire.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's what I was looking for, but a different document was provided for the witness. At least the document that I saw lying in front of him was not the document that I had requested.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I can assist the registrar. I believe this was also raised earlier that there was a page missing. If it would help for the Prosecution to give the Prosecution's copy, we'd be happy to.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Registry apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Zorc, sir, you've looked at this document before, haven't you? This is a report by the 9th Military Naval Sector command concerning damage in Dubrovnik's Old Town. This report was sent directly to the deputy federal secretary for national defence, Admiral Stane Brovet, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, sir, first of all: Before you wrote your expert opinion, did you have an opportunity to see this document?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not believe of having seen it earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, sir, my question is the same as in relation to the document dated the 7th of December, 1991. If you look at this document, is there any kind of reference or anything to suggest that it was sent to the command of the 2nd Operational Group or to the attention of the command of the 2nd Operational Group, so they may familiarise themselves with the substance?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. We cannot infer that on the basis of this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My next question in relation to this document is perhaps of a more technical nature. I don't believe it should present any serious difficulty to you. From the point of view of the doctrine governing command and control, can you tell me, who does this document belong to? Whose document is it?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document of the 9th Naval Sector command dated 9th of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would that mean that that particular command and its commander were the ones who issued this document?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Wrote it, signed it, and issued it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, sir: By putting his signature there and by denoting his rank and his official position, does that mean that the commander is endorsing this report?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we therefore say that the commander is in agreement with this report, since we see that he has signed it and sent it on to a superior command?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you cannot conclude that from that report. In this report, the commander of the 9th VPS transfers and sends the findings of the commission he has set up and which has determined certain damage to individual sites. Does he stand behind this report or not and its content? Nothing is said about that in the document. He just states that this is the report of that group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, sir: If you look at that document, are there any signatures anywhere or anything that might resemble the original substance of a report drafted by some three-man commission?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There's no signature of these members of the commission, while the contents certainly arise from the report of that commission. Everything is specified in detail. And the commander who signed this report indicates that the situation, as it has been determined, was determined by the commission which he formed, and he also specifies who was in the commission and when. And he states that the situation was determined by the commission, which made a report, submitted to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we discern whose commission it was?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I already stated that. It's also said in the document. It is a commission of the 9th VPS. It is a commission of General Jokic. And also, as far as the previous question is concerned, whether he stands behind the content of this report, I can only add that he does stand. It's not explicitly stated, but if he personally doubted the precision of the report, he would certainly indicate that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the core of the matter. That is what I really wanted to ask you about. As corps commander, that is to say, without a signature, without the signatures of the members of a commission, would you sign a report that they had submitted and send it further on to the higher command if you did not agree with it?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if the request was made, I would send the report, and I would draw the attention that I do not agree with it. That can happen. But, you know, if I didn't agree with a report, I wouldn't even accept such a report from a commission.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's just clarify one more thing there. You identified who it was who established the commission. It was the command of the 9th Military Naval Sector and its commander; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's stated in the document -- in this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean, then, that the command of the 9th VPS and its commander gave a task to the commission and instructions in terms of what the commission was supposed to do?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me one more thing now. As regards such a document and the report that you have in front of you - I'm asking you hypothetically now - had you established a commission and given it precise instructions as to what it was supposed to do, given it a precise task, can there ultimately be a situation that the commission does compile a report in accordance with the task that you gave them, and that they sign such a report, and that you send on that kind of report only with an accompanying letter on your part to the superior command?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is also quite possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would there be a significant difference involved, then, between two such documents?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As far as its significance goes, no. But it would be a more rapid process. But with this accompanying letter, the commander of the 9th VPS would take upon himself also a part of the responsibility for it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at any rate, if I understood you correctly, the command stands by that document?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We will no longer be needing this document. General Zorc, I would like to ask you the following now: How does the principle of singleness of command operate in practice, as well as subordination, upon which the military organisation in the JNA is based? Can you explain this to me at the level of a corps and brigade and in relations between commands of brigades and commands of corps, and the other way around?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The system of command and control, on all levels, also at the level of commands of corps, with its subordinate unit, operate on the basis of the principle of singleness of command. It means that the commander of the corps is the sole [as interpreted] and the superior and that the corps commander is the only competent one to issue direct tasks, assignments, to him. Here I must warn -- draw your attention that also the superior officers have the right to issue tasks to the second lower level, or even more, but these are exceptions. This should be avoided. Now, if we look at the position of the brigade commander and singleness of command, it means that his superior commander, from which he may receive orders, is the corps commander. And in the command of the corps, and outside of it, there are no other officers who could have commanding authority. As far as the chain of command is concerned on these two levels, the relationship between the corps commander and the brigade commander, it is a direct relationship. Would that be enough?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Can you tell me: To what command level does a corps commander issue orders? Let me put a specific question. Is that the brigade commander, the first one down the chain of command?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Corps commander issues reports -- orders to his directly subordinate commanders, the first level. The commanders who are in direct subordination to the corps commander, they are in different levels, and this can be on the level of the brigade, commander of brigade, but the first subordinate to the corps commander, the commander of the independent battalion, regiment or company. So irrespective of the size of the subordinate unit, if it is the first level subordinate to the corps commander, he then issues the orders to them directly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we understand it, then, in the following way: That each commander is responsible to his direct superior officer for those who are his first, direct subordinates?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you pose this question once again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is each commander responsible to his immediate superior officer for the person who is his immediate subordinate?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I've understood the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you try to answer, then?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I understood you now, your question. Well, clearly, any unit commander is answerable to his first superior commander, but not only for their first subordinates, but all of his subordinates, the entire unit. And in his unit, he has different levels, down to the platoon levels. As an example, let me say that the brigade commander is answerable to the corps commander, not only for the battalion commanders but for the entire battalions. This is the essence. And, of course, for other independent units of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please -- perhaps I did not understand this well. But would it mean, then, according to that logic, that the federal secretary is responsible for his very last soldier?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're thinking of the command responsibility, then yes, the federal secretary is responsible for all the units under his subordination. And when you've asked about the federal secretary, I must add that, on the basis of the command authority, he received this command authority from the supreme commander, that is, the Presidency. So this is a limitation here, but for lower-ranking units, the answer is simpler.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you a specific question. Do you know, from your own practice -- for example, was an army commander or a military district commander held accountable for any mistake or criminal offence that had been committed by the commander of some battalion in that army or military district, or a company commander, if we are going all the way down the chain? If you know of such a case, could you please tell me of that specific example.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The responsibility of the brigade commander to his superior, when speaking of the brigade, the chief of General Staff was his superior. And in connection with one of your previous questions, the subordinate, how their superiors are responsible, I -- let me say neither -- didn't know about these responsibilities. But I assume that they were called in for and were responsible in that sense. If it were of any help to you, I do know of a case when a brigade commander was called in for -- to -- and was answerable because something happened in a company, a grave accident, so they can be called in and are answerable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you -- now, I don't know if it's a question of interpretation, whether it was a misinterpretation. I was asking you about the level of the commander of an army or a military district. Did you ever, in your years of service, hear of an army commander being held accountable for any kind of mistake made or criminal offence committed by a company commander or a battalion commander, and if that battalion or company was within his army?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I stated that I'm not acquainted with such a case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that a convenient time, Mr. Rodic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We've moved fairly slowly today. I trust you'll keep that in mind on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will, Your Honour. I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will resume, then, at 2.15 on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
